title: Water Fill Timeout
shortDescription: The dishwasher did not reach the target water level in time.
fullDescription:
E1 is raised when the flow meter or pressure switch does not register adequate fill within the allowed time. A closed supply tap, kinked inlet hose, clogged inlet filter, or failed inlet valve are all common causes.

Check the tap first, then the inlet screen at the back of the dishwasher.

causes.cause: Supply tap closed or partly open

fixSteps.title: Check tap
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure the supply tap is fully open.

fixSteps.title: Clean filter
fixSteps.instruction: Unscrew inlet hose and rinse the mesh filter.

fixSteps.title: Replace valve
fixSteps.instruction: If fill is still slow, replace the inlet valve.

whenToCallPro: If the valve tests good and the fault returns - board may be at fault.

faq.q: Why does it fill then stop?
faq.a: Low water pressure can cause intermittent E1 - verify at least 1 bar at the tap.

title: Water Heating Fault
shortDescription: The dishwasher did not reach wash temperature within the time limit.
fullDescription:
E3 means the NTC sensor has not seen the target temperature rise within the expected window. A failed heating element or relay, open thermal fuse, or bad NTC sensor cause this.

Start by testing the heating element resistance - typically 20-40 ohm.

fixSteps.title: Test heater
fixSteps.instruction: Measure the heating element resistance - open means replace.

fixSteps.title: Replace heater
fixSteps.instruction: Swap the flow-through heater assembly if open.

whenToCallPro: If you are not comfortable with internal plumbing.

faq.a: Some models allow a cold Quick wash; check your manual.

title: Over-temperature
shortDescription: Wash water temperature exceeded the safe limit.
fullDescription:
E4 indicates the NTC read above the maximum allowed temperature, typically 75 °C. A welded heater relay or stuck control board keeps the heater on.

Turn off the breaker and inspect the control board before running another cycle.

fixSteps.title: Replace control
fixSteps.instruction: Swap the main control board to clear welded relay.

faq.a: Plastic items can warp; ceramic and glass usually survive.

title: Temperature Sensor Open
shortDescription: The wash water temperature sensor reads open circuit.
fullDescription:
H1 is posted when the NTC in the sump reads infinite resistance. A broken sensor or disconnected plug are the usual causes.

Replacement is straightforward on most models - remove the kick panel and access the sump.

fixSteps.title: Access sump
fixSteps.instruction: Remove kick panel to reach sump sensor connector.

whenToCallPro: If you would rather not tip the unit.

faq.a: Most models refuse to start on H1.

title: Temperature Sensor Short
shortDescription: The wash water temperature sensor reads shorted.
fullDescription:
H3 is the shorted counterpart of H1. The NTC or its wiring reads near zero ohms, so the control thinks the water is extremely hot and disables heating.

Replace the NTC and inspect wiring for pinching near the sump.
whenToCallPro: If wiring damage is inside the body.

faq.a: A shorted heater could drop voltage at the NTC line - inspect together.

title: Leak / Anti-flood Trip
shortDescription: The base-pan float has detected water and the anti-flood system has activated.
fullDescription:
LE is raised when the float switch in the base pan lifts due to leaked water. The drain pump runs continuously to remove it and the dishwasher refuses to restart.

Find the leak - common sources are the door seal, sump, recirc pump seal, and hose clamps - before drying out the base pan.

fixSteps.title: Unplug
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect power and turn off water.

fixSteps.title: Dry base pan
fixSteps.instruction: Tilt and absorb water with towels.

fixSteps.title: Locate leak
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect door seal, sump, hose clamps, and softener cap.

whenToCallPro: If the leak source is not visible.

faq.a: No - LE returns immediately if the base pan is still wet.

title: Communication Error
shortDescription: Main control and user interface boards are not communicating.
fullDescription:
AE indicates a loss of communication between the top-door control panel and the base main control. Water ingress into the door harness is the most frequent cause, followed by a failed board.

Power cycle first; if AE persists, inspect the door hinge harness for corrosion.

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness
fixSteps.instruction: Remove door panel and check hinge wiring.

faq.a: Often yes, especially within the first 24 months.

title: Drain Pump Fault
shortDescription: Water was not drained within the allowed time.
fullDescription:
E5 is posted when the drain pump runs but the pressure or flow sensor does not indicate drop in level. A clogged filter, kinked drain hose, or failed pump are typical causes.

Clean the filter cup in the sump and check the drain line for obstructions.

fixSteps.title: Clean filter
fixSteps.instruction: Twist out the filter cup and rinse thoroughly.

fixSteps.title: Check hose
fixSteps.instruction: Unkink drain hose and verify high-loop installation.

fixSteps.title: Replace pump
fixSteps.instruction: If water still remains, swap the drain pump.

whenToCallPro: If the pump tests good but drain still fails.

faq.a: Yes - prevents dirty sink water siphoning back.

title: Wash Motor Fault
shortDescription: The recirculation wash pump is not running at the commanded speed.
fullDescription:
E6 indicates the BLDC wash motor tacho is missing or the motor is drawing too much current. A jammed impeller, broken glass in the sump, or failed motor are typical causes.

Remove the filter cup and inspect the impeller for debris before replacing the motor.

fixSteps.title: Clear impeller
fixSteps.instruction: Remove filter and inspect sump impeller for debris.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: Fit a new wash pump assembly if still faulty.

whenToCallPro: If tipping the unit is required.

faq.a: Yes - pre-rinse and avoid dropping glass shards into the sump.

title: Diverter Valve Fault
shortDescription: The spray-arm diverter did not reach its commanded position.
fullDescription:
Multi-level wash models use a diverter valve to alternate between upper and lower spray arms. E7 is posted when the diverter position feedback is missing or wrong, often because the diverter motor has failed.

The diverter is part of the sump assembly and typically requires tipping the dishwasher.

fixSteps.title: Clean sump
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect sump for debris around diverter.

faq.a: Only one rack will clean properly.
